doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Hanging out with Barry Harris, Donald Byrd and the Conyers brothers
summary: Foster's circle in Detroit included Harris, Byrd and Sonny Red, and hipsters like Nathan Conyers.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Barry Harris was around. Barry and I and Donald Byrd, Sonny Red, we used to hang together a lot during those days.
I think a couple years back I remember you getting an award -- by the way did you know John Conyers at that time? Was he on the scene?
I didn’t know Conyers, but the Conyers family had about three or four brothers. I used to hang out with one of them, Nathan Conyers.
That’s the one that owns the car dealership, that’s where you guys -­
Oh, yeah? He and I used to -­
In fact he’s one of the premier -- he has one of the largest -- African- Americans -- one of the largest car dealership businesses in the country.
Is that right? I hadn’t seen him since that period. I hadn’t seen him all through the ’50s, ’60s. I never saw him again after leaving Detroit.
Was he on the music scene or you just kind of knew him?
Well he was one of the so-called hipsters, the guys who appreciated the music, as was John. There was another brother whose name I can’t recall. We just hung out together.
